purpose: Pedagogical distinctions for annotation scope, not a new unseen performance benchmark.
provenance: Original fictional teaching text authored after inspecting the paired trial and label review, then revised through one independent reviewer's initial label-free review and two targeted rechecks. Later reviews were informed by earlier findings. This is development agreement, not expert gold validation or a fresh held-out evaluation. No candidate was run on these examples.
usage_limits: Do not treat labels as externally validated gold.
Do not use these examples to claim model improvement or qualification.
Do not silently relabel the frozen paired trial.
All reasoning-critical context is repeated in each case.
This review-sidecar format is not a change to the frozen evaluator schema.
P01B and P02A deliberately reuse one context-claim anchor; the 30 rows contain 29 unique inputs and are not independent observations.
The three draft semantic classes are unchanged. Material ambiguity or same-target conflict receives a separate review_needed disposition and no semantic label.

pairs.topic: Direct narration versus reported world fact
pairs.controlled_change: Replace the direct assertion with an attributed report.
Keep the context identical and change only the claim target.
Add an explicit guarantee about the quoted proposition.
Add an explicit guarantee about the reported lever state.
Remove only the report wrapper around the negative proposition.
Change the exact proposition guaranteed true and explicitly leave the other time assertion unaddressed.

pairs.topic: Mixed direct facts and reported event
pairs.controlled_change: Add a truth bridge for the report of two pen-removal events.

pairs.topic: Reported starting quantity versus direct quantity
pairs.controlled_change: Change only the starting quantity from report to narration.
Add the marker's membership at the required time.

pairs.topic: Outside the domain is not a negative conclusion
pairs.controlled_change: Change only K's location relative to the rule domain.
Keep the context identical and narrow only the claim's time interval.
Add that the same person held the role throughout the interval.

pairs.topic: Joined reported accounts versus world conclusion
pairs.controlled_change: Keep the context identical and change only the target to a consequence of both accounts.
Keep the context identical and change only the target attribution level.

cases.context: Fictional scenario. Narrator fact: At 12:00 the desk held exactly nine pens. Narrator fact: The accounting interval covers every inventory change after the initial count at 12:00 up to and including the final count at 13:00. The final count at 13:00 is taken after all inventory changes occurring at 13:00, and all of those changes are included in the accounting interval. In this scenario, the count at 13:00 means that final count. A note says, "During the whole accounting interval defined above, exactly two distinct pens were removed from the desk, each exactly once." The quoted note ends here. Narrator fact: No pens were added to the desk at any time during the whole accounting interval, including no return of any removed pen. At most two pen-removal events occurred during that whole interval, each removing one pen. Narrator fact: Throughout the whole accounting interval, counted pens retain their identities and remain pens, and the desk's pen count changes only through additions or removals.
cases.claim: The desk held exactly seven pens at 13:00.
evidence_spans: Narrator fact: At 12:00 the desk held exactly nine pens.

Narrator fact: The accounting interval covers every inventory change after the initial count at 12:00 up to and including the final count at 13:00. The final count at 13:00 is taken after all inventory changes occurring at 13:00, and all of those changes are included in the accounting interval. In this scenario, the count at 13:00 means that final count.
A note says, "During the whole accounting interval defined above, exactly two distinct pens were removed from the desk, each exactly once." The quoted note ends here.

Narrator fact: No pens were added to the desk at any time during the whole accounting interval, including no return of any removed pen. At most two pen-removal events occurred during that whole interval, each removing one pen.
Narrator fact: Throughout the whole accounting interval, counted pens retain their identities and remain pens, and the desk's pen count changes only through additions or removals.
cases.rationale: The initial count is nine. All changes through the final count are covered; no additions and at most two one-pen removals are stipulated. The note alone cannot establish exactly two actual removals, so seven, eight, or nine pens can remain.

cases.context: Fictional scenario. A label says, "There are exactly eight beads in the jar at 14:00." The quoted label ends here. Narrator fact: The accounting interval covers every inventory change after the initial count at 14:00 up to and including the final count at 15:00. The final count at 15:00 is taken after all inventory changes occurring at 15:00, and all of those changes are included in the accounting interval. In this scenario, the count at 15:00 means that final count. Narrator fact: During the whole accounting interval, exactly three distinct beads were removed from the jar, each in a single one-bead removal event. No bead-removal events occurred anywhere in that whole interval besides these three events. Narrator fact: No beads were added to the jar at any time during the whole accounting interval, including no return of any of the three removed beads. Narrator fact: Throughout the whole accounting interval, counted beads retain their identities and remain beads, and the jar's bead count changes only through additions or removals.
cases.claim: There were exactly five beads in the jar at 15:00.
evidence_spans: A label says, "There are exactly eight beads in the jar at 14:00." The quoted label ends here.

Narrator fact: The accounting interval covers every inventory change after the initial count at 14:00 up to and including the final count at 15:00. The final count at 15:00 is taken after all inventory changes occurring at 15:00, and all of those changes are included in the accounting interval. In this scenario, the count at 15:00 means that final count.

Narrator fact: During the whole accounting interval, exactly three distinct beads were removed from the jar, each in a single one-bead removal event. No bead-removal events occurred anywhere in that whole interval besides these three events.
Narrator fact: No beads were added to the jar at any time during the whole accounting interval, including no return of any of the three removed beads.
Narrator fact: Throughout the whole accounting interval, counted beads retain their identities and remain beads, and the jar's bead count changes only through additions or removals.

Marker K is in the courtyard at noon.

cases.context: Fictional scenario. Narrator fact: Sheet A and Sheet B refer to the same bowl on the same day. Sheet A says, "The bowl contains exactly twelve buttons at 10:00." Sheet B says, "The accounting interval covers every inventory change after the initial count at 10:00 up to and including the final count at 11:00. The final count at 11:00 is taken after all inventory changes occurring at 11:00, and all of those changes are included in the accounting interval. In this account, the count at 11:00 means that final count. During the whole accounting interval, exactly four distinct buttons were removed from the bowl, each in a single one-button removal event. No button-removal events occurred anywhere in that whole interval besides these four events. No buttons were added to the bowl at any time during the whole accounting interval, including no return of any of the four removed buttons. Throughout the whole accounting interval, counted buttons retain their identities and remain buttons, and the bowl's button count changes only through additions or removals."
cases.claim: The bowl contained exactly eight buttons at 11:00.
evidence_spans: Narrator fact: Sheet A and Sheet B refer to the same bowl on the same day.
Sheet A says, "The bowl contains exactly twelve buttons at 10:00."

Sheet B says, "The accounting interval covers every inventory change after the initial count at 10:00 up to and including the final count at 11:00. The final count at 11:00 is taken after all inventory changes occurring at 11:00, and all of those changes are included in the accounting interval. In this account, the count at 11:00 means that final count. During the whole accounting interval, exactly four distinct buttons were removed from the bowl, each in a single one-button removal event. No button-removal events occurred anywhere in that whole interval besides these four events. No buttons were added to the bowl at any time during the whole accounting interval, including no return of any of the four removed buttons. Throughout the whole accounting interval, counted buttons retain their identities and remain buttons, and the bowl's button count changes only through additions or removals."
cases.rationale: The narrator establishes only the shared bowl and day. The starting count and every interval, event, exclusion, and transition premise remain within the two reported accounts. No applicable truth guarantee establishes the world's final count.
